finding: capability_url_targets_the_kinds_listing_surface asserts the origin-collapsed probe URL the rewritten Unknown branch no longer produces; cargo test --lib -p ziee llm_repository:: fails.
resolution: Verified RED by running: left Some("http://127.0.0.1:1520/models/api/models?limit=1") vs right Some("http://127.0.0.1:1520/api/models?limit=1"). The IMPLEMENTATION is correct (beae7c7fb deliberately preserves the row's path); the test and its comment were left on the old behaviour. Updated the expectation, corrected the now-false NOTE claiming the probe URL is kind-derived, and added two missing cases (HF row WITH a path segment gets author=; Unknown row with NO path keeps the bare-origin probe).

finding: The missing-`spec` refusal hands back BACKGROUND_SPEC_EXAMPLE (a spec-LEVEL object with no `spec` key), contradicting the comment three lines above it; every_spawn_refusal_is_actionable panics.
resolution: Verified RED by running. The comment states the requirement exactly ('must be a full ARGUMENTS object, not a spec-level one') and the code violates it — the comment described the fix that was never applied. Changed to default_example(), which is the full arguments object; both suites now 71 passed / 0 failed.

finding: resolve_server_and_tool discards a well-formed <server_uuid>__<tool> prefix whenever the per-message map cannot UNIQUELY confirm the bare name, so a correctly-composed name for a tool two attached servers both advertise resolves to (None, tool) and is refused.
resolution: REAL, and re-read at mcp.rs:427-443 to confirm: map is HashMap<String,Option<Uuid>> and collapses an ambiguous bare name to None, so recover_server_id_for_bare_name(name,map) != Some(sid) and line 442 returns None even though the prefix identified the owner unambiguously. NOT fixed here, deliberately. This is upstream's own deliberate refuse-over-misroute tradeoff, stated in the SECURITY (B-OWN) comment at mcp.rs:430-438, and the failure mode is a clear refusal, never a misroute or a wrong answer. A correct fix needs the map to retain WHICH servers advertise a name rather than collapsing to None — a change to shared, security-sensitive routing that would fork paws from upstream on exactly the axis this task exists to avoid. Escalated to the owner to take upstream instead.

finding: In test_repository_connection_by_id the cross-target secret guard is nested inside `if let Some(form_auth) = overrides.auth_config`, so a request overriding ONLY `url` keeps the persisted decrypted credential and the probe sends it to the caller-chosen host.
resolution: PRE-EXISTING in BOTH repos and OUT OF SCOPE for this port. Verified: `url_changed` is computed then left unused on the no-auth_config path at handlers.rs:584-585 here AND at handlers.rs:564 on paws origin/main; this branch's only change to this file is +20 lines in the OTHER function (test_repository_connection, the unsaved path). So the port neither introduces nor worsens it. Fixing an unrelated credential-exfiltration bug inside a port PR is scope creep that deserves its own branch and its own regression test. ESCALATED to the owner as a separate item.

finding: create_session_tracked opens the per-server breaker on ANY McpSession::new error, not only unreachability, and the breaker is keyed by server_id alone — so one user's authorization failure suppresses the server for every other user.
resolution: Upstream's design, ported faithfully. Real limitation, but changing the breaker's key or its failure classification is a behavioural fork of shared code. Reported upstream rather than patched here.

finding: Nothing clears a server's breaker entry when its row is edited, so a corrected URL/credential is still refused from cache for up to the 5-minute cooldown.
resolution: Upstream's design, ported faithfully. Same rationale as the row above; reported upstream.

finding: Terminal reconciliation reaches only workflow-backed runs; the chat-hosted agent path (the other PgTaskListStore consumer, keyed by message id) has no reconcile call and cannot match the boot sweep's join on workflow_runs.id.
resolution: A SCOPE LIMIT of upstream's fix, not a defect the port introduces — the leak it does close (41/88 rig rows) is real and this branch delivers it. Widening it to the chat path is new feature work on shared code. Reported upstream.

finding: The new reconcile step propagates with `?` ahead of the pre-existing staging-directory GC, so a DB error in the new secondary write now aborts cleanup that previously ran.
resolution: Upstream's, and low impact (the caller only logs; the GC runs again next boot). Reported upstream rather than diverged.

finding: misplaced_kind_error always names other.required_field as the supplied field, so a call that misplaced the other kind's OPTIONAL field is told to remove a field it never sent.
resolution: Upstream message-quality defect, ported faithfully. Cosmetic in effect (the refusal is still correct, only the named field is wrong). Reported upstream.

finding: Making a well-formed <uuid>__tool name depend on the per-turn bare_name_map widens the blast radius of the global MAX_PENDING_TOOL_MAPS eviction (a guard.clear() of ALL users' maps) from prefix-less names to every tool call.
resolution: Same root cause as the high-severity row above and the same disposition: upstream's design, fail-closed (a refusal, never a misroute), escalated rather than forked. Counted as the corroborating second angle on that finding.

finding: parse_non_streaming_response_body newly routes a non-SSE-labelled body into extract_response_by_id, whose debug log slices a third-party string by BYTE index and can panic mid-codepoint.
resolution: Upstream's, and gated on the operator enabling `debug` for that target (default is `info`), so it degrades one tool call rather than the service. Reported upstream.

finding: is_usable_repository_base's doc claims the capability probe 'necessarily queries that kind's fixed API host … NOT the row's own URL' and that Unknown's 'probe already targets its own origin' — both made false by beae7c7fb.
resolution: Rewritten to state that capability_probe_url now grades the ROW (author=<org> for HF, own PATH for Unknown), and that this guard constrains URL shape rather than being the only thing between a bogus row and healthy.

finding: The same function records the nonexistent-org problem as a 'KNOWN GAP … out of scope here' and names `…/api/models?author=<org>` as the fix that would close it — but that fix shipped in the same commit.
resolution: Rewritten to say the gap is CLOSED and where, and to keep the still-true reason the fix lives in capability_probe_url rather than in this guard (an origin-only guard here was tried and rejected because it reports every legitimate org-scoped row unverified).

finding: capability_probe_url's OWN doc still says the Unknown branch probes 'the repository's OWN origin', contradicting its body and the assertion round 1 corrected.
resolution: Doc now describes the real behaviour for all three kinds, including the HF author filter and the reason Unknown appends to the PATH (that path is the base the download path uses, so an origin probe grades a URL that path never touches).
